sections.h2: Which Fulton County offices handle my tax bill?
sections.html:
Two offices share the job. The Board of Assessors values the land and buildings. The Tax Commissioner then turns that value into a bill and collects the money.

The Tax Commissioner collects for the county government, the Fulton County and Atlanta school systems, the State of Georgia, and five cities: Atlanta, Mountain Park, Sandy Springs, Johns Creek and Chattahoochee Hills. If your house sits in another Fulton city, expect that city to run its own bill. Every levy appears on its own line because each body picks its own rate.

A house in dense Sandy Springs and one in rural Chattahoochee Hills can land in very different tax situations, so read the parcel on your own bill before relying on any county average.

The Tax Commissioner runs several walk-in centers. Four of them post weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the phone line is 404-613-6100.

  • Government Center downtown: 141 Pryor Street SW, Suite 1113, Atlanta 30303.
  • Maxwell Road center: 11575 Maxwell Road, Alpharetta 30022.
  • North Fulton center: 7741 Roswell Road NE, Sandy Springs 30350.
  • South Fulton center: 5600 Stonewall Tell Road, College Park 30349.
  • Greenbriar Mall center: 2841 Greenbriar Parkway, Suite 124, Atlanta 30331.

For valuation or exemption questions, the Board of Assessors takes calls at 404-612-6440 and email at boa@fultoncountyga.gov, with its main office at 141 Pryor Street, Suite 1018. You can look up and pay a bill at fultoncountytaxes.org, and assessment notices are posted at fultonassessor.org.

sections.h2: Due dates, bills and late charges
sections.html:
Dates shift from year to year. For 2026, notices of assessment appeared online June 19 and bills went out August 15. The state had not yet certified the digest, so the county asked the Superior Court of Fulton County for a temporary collection order and billed at the 2025 millage rates. A revised bill or a refund follows only when final rates differ from the temporary ones.

Fulton County property tax calendar
StepRule or date
Homestead exemption filingApril 1 standard deadline; a second window opens during the appeal period
Appeal an assessmentWithin 45 days of the notice date
2026 bills mailedAugust 15, 2026
City of Atlanta tax dueSeptember 30, 2026
Fulton County and other jurisdictions dueOctober 15, 2026
Late paymentInterest from the next day; 5% penalty at day 120, repeating every 120 days to a 20% cap

If you plan to sell, find out from the Tax Commissioner whether the parcel carries a temporary or final bill, and have your settlement agent explain how any later adjustment is divided.

Your appeal window is 45 days from the date stamped on the notice. Only the assessed value can be challenged, because the estimated tax amount is off limits.

You can submit online at fultonassessor.org, mail it in, or hand it over at a Board of Assessors office. The filing form asks you to pick among three routes: a Board of Equalization hearing, arbitration that is non-binding and covers valuation alone, or a Hearing Officer. Arbitration and the officer route may involve fees. Plan on several months, and keep paying any temporary bill that arrives meanwhile, because skipped payments add penalties.

You can raise taxability, value, uniformity, or a denied exemption. The state revenue agency cannot overrule a local board on a single appraisal.

sections.h2: What to bring to the assessors
sections.html:
Whether you call the Board of Assessors or file online, have your parcel number and the notice in front of you. Add recent sales of similar houses nearby, photos of any damage or deferred repairs, and a repair estimate if the house needs work. A buyer's inspection report can also show a condition problem the county could not see from the street.

Write down the notice date as soon as it arrives. Everything else in the process, including the choice among equalization, arbitration and a Hearing Officer, runs from that date, and the three routes differ in cost and speed. Ask which one fits a dispute over value alone before you commit.

A homestead exemption knocks down the taxable value of the house where you live. Georgia's baseline exemption is $2,000 of assessed value, and many counties stack larger ones on top.

Fulton added school-tax exemptions in 2026 with no income test:

  • Fulton County School District: 25% of assessed value is exempt once the owner is 65 by January 1, and 50% once the owner is 70.
  • To qualify there, you must have held a homestead exemption in that district for at least 5 of the last 6 years.
  • Atlanta Public Schools district: up to $50,000 comes off assessed value when the owner turned 65 by January 1, and it can be paired with other APS exemptions.

These apply to school levies only. Owners who already have a basic exemption and fit the new criteria get the discount applied without refiling. If you did not own on January 1, apply the next year. An owner who qualifies but misses April 1 may be able to apply during the appeal period.

sections.h2: Settling the tax bill when you sell
sections.html:
The owner on January 1 carries the whole year's tax. Georgia gives no partial refund when someone sells and moves, so any split with the buyer comes from the contract language.

The state's formula is (assessed value minus $2,000) times the millage rate, with assessed value fixed at 40% of fair market value. Fulton's bill breaks the county, school and city rates apart, so check each line.

  1. Search your parcel on the county tax site and confirm nothing is overdue.
  2. If money is owed, ask the Tax Commissioner for a payoff amount.
  3. Hand the payoff to whoever prepares your settlement statement.

County tax liens go on the clerk's general execution docket, and unpaid taxes are best cleared before a sale. A cash sale still runs through a title search, so the payoff is handled the same way.

Fulton County has 1,098,791 residents and 534,663 housing units across 526.70 square miles of land. Owners live in 54.3% of the county's homes, and the median owner-occupied value is $458,800. Median gross rent is $1,732.

With renters in about 46% of homes, tenant-occupied houses and properties needing work are everyday cases in Fulton, and each changes the timing of a sale. Builders pulled 9,660 permits in 2025.

faqs.q: When does Fulton County collect property tax?
faqs.a: The dates change by year and by jurisdiction. In 2026 the City of Atlanta's share was due September 30 and everything else, including county and school levies, was due October 15. Your own bill prints the date, and the Tax Commissioner at 404-613-6100 can confirm it.

faqs.q: What happens if I pay Fulton County tax late?
faqs.a: Interest begins the next day and runs until you pay. A 5% penalty lands on day 120, and another 5% every 120 days after, up to 20%. The office takes partial payments, though interest continues on whatever principal remains.

faqs.q: Can the person who bought my house still appeal the value?
faqs.a: Only the owner named on the notice can appeal, and the notice date starts a 45-day clock. If you sell before the next notice, ask your settlement agent who files for that year.

faqs.q: Does the seller or buyer pay Fulton County tax at closing?
faqs.a: The contract divides it. The January 1 owner carries the full year, and a seller who leaves mid-year gets no state refund. The settlement statement shows how your deal handled the split.

faqs.q: How do I get a homestead exemption in Fulton County?
faqs.a: Apply with the Board of Assessors. April 1 is the normal cutoff, and a second window opens during the 45-day appeal period. Anyone who bought after January 1 files for the following year. Call 404-612-6440 to confirm your case.
